mainTopic: Lashes for a single warning (סומכוס), the seller's duty to warn about אותו ואת בנו on festival eves, acquiring the butcher's ox, and how the 'one day' of אותו ואת בנו is counted.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about נותר. רבי יהודה says there are no lashes only because a positive command follows the prohibition, while רבי יעקב says it is because no action is involved. Next the גמרא tries to prove how סומכוס counts lashes, using a ברייתא about eating two גידי הנשה, but it rejects the proof: רבי יהודה's 'only forty' may simply be because one גיד was smaller than a כזית. A new משנה follows. On four festival eves, a seller must tell the buyer if he sold the mother or offspring of the animal for slaughter. On those days the butcher can also be forced to slaughter, and if the ox dies, the buyer takes the loss. The גמרא explains that the buyer may rely on the seller's silence, and why the groom gets the mother and the bride the daughter. It then asks how the buyer can lose an ox he never pulled. It gives two answers: someone acquired the meat for him because it was to his benefit, or on these days the חכמים let the Torah law stand, under which money acquires. Finally, a new משנה teaches that for אותו ואת בנו the day follows the night. בן זומא learns this from the words 'one day' in the creation story, even though the section deals with קדשים.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: no lashes for leftovers because a positive command follows the prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא about leaving over meat ends with רבי יהודה's reason for no lashes: the Torah added a positive command to burn the leftovers. That implies he would give lashes otherwise, even with an uncertain warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse comes to give a positive command right after a prohibition, to teach that one is not lashed for it. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: We are at the end of a quoted ברייתא. רבי יהודה explains that the only reason there are no lashes for leaving over the meat is that the Torah gave a positive command to burn it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse first forbids leaving the meat until morning, then commands burning whatever is left. Since a לאו that can be fixed by a positive command (לאו הניתק לעשה) gets no lashes, that is רבי יהודה's reason. The point being drawn is that he needed this special reason, so he would otherwise give lashes even though the warning here is an uncertain one (התראת ספק).

keyTerms.meaning: A positive commandment, something you must do
A prohibition, something you must not do
They give lashes (מלקות)
A prohibition that can be fixed by doing a positive command, so it carries no lashes
An uncertain warning, given when it is not yet clear the sin will happen

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not saying leaving over meat is permitted. It is still forbidden; he is only explaining why בית דין does not give lashes for it.

phrases.english: The verse comes to give a positive commandment
phrases.notes: שמות 12:10

phrases.english: after a prohibition,
to say that one is not lashed for it,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא הַכָּתוּב לִיתֵּן עֲשֵׂה אַחַר לֹא תַּעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא that was quoted before this section began.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה holds that an uncertain warning (התראת ספק) can still lead to lashes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on נותר: רבי יהודה needs the special reason of עשה אחר לא תעשה to exempt from lashes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are no lashes for נותר because the Torah gave a positive command to burn it after the prohibition.

steps.title: רבי יעקב: no lashes because leaving meat over involves no action
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב gives a different reason for no lashes: leaving meat over is a prohibition with no action, and such a prohibition never gets lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב says: That is not the reason. The reason is that this is a prohibition with no action, and for any prohibition with no action, one is not lashed.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא in the same ברייתא agrees there are no lashes but gives a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יעקב, the sin of נותר is just failing to finish the meat in time. Nothing is actually done. Since a לאו שאין בו מעשה never gets lashes, he does not need the 'positive command' reason at all.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not for that reason
A prohibition broken without doing any physical action

phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov says:
This is not for that reason,
rather, it is because it is
a prohibition that has no action in it,
and any prohibition that has no action in it,
one is not lashed for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִן הַשֵּׁם הוּא זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רבי יהודה's reason while agreeing there are no lashes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are no lashes for a prohibition that involves no action, and that is why there are none for נותר.

steps.title: A new source: eating two sciatic nerves from two animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: someone who ate two גידי הנשה from two animals gets eighty lashes. רבי יהודה says only forty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone ate two גידין from two thighs of two animals, he gets eighty lashes. רבי יהודה says he gets only forty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to help with the question about סומכוס. This step only sets out the source; the next steps work out what it proves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two גידין means two separate forbidden items. The תנא קמא counts two sets of lashes (40 + 40 = 80), while רבי יהודה counts only one. The גמרא will first figure out exactly what case this is: separate eatings, or one eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Sinews, here the גיד הנשה (sciatic nerve) that may not be eaten
Thighs
Receives (lashes); literally 'absorbs'
Eighty / forty: two sets of lashes versus one set

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If one ate two sciatic nerves
from two thighs of two animals,
he receives eighty lashes;
phrases.notes: The usual set of lashes counts as forty, so eighty means two sets.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
he receives only forty.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אָכַל שְׁנֵי גִידִין מִשְּׁתֵּי יְרֵכוֹת מִשְּׁתֵּי בְהֵמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the נותר ברייתא to a new source about the question regarding סומכוס.
steps.raayaObject: How סומכוס counts lashes for two eatings under one warning.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about eating two גידי הנשה.

steps.title: What case is the ברייתא talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case is. If he ate them one after the other with two warnings, רבי יהודה's 'only forty' would make no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say he ate them one after the other, with two warnings, then what is רבי יהודה's reason for saying forty and no more?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to pin down the exact case of the ברייתא and rules out the first option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate eatings with two separate warnings are clearly two separate sins, and everyone would give two sets of lashes. Since רבי יהודה gives only forty, that cannot be the case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?
If you say (a suggestion about to be rejected)
One after the other
Warnings given before a sin; needed for lashes
And no more

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say he ate them one after the other
and with two warnings,
what is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda
who says: forty and no more?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה וּבִשְׁתֵּי הַתְרָאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the case of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the two גידין were eaten separately with two warnings or together with one warning.

steps.title: It must be one eating with one warning
steps.stepSummary: The case must be that he ate both גידין at the same time after a single warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that he ate them at the same time, with one warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the ברייתא is about eating both together after one warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only with one act and one warning does רבי יהודה's 'only forty' make sense. That means the תנא קמא gives eighty even with just one warning, which is the key point for the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
At the same time, in one act
One warning

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious: at the same time
and with one warning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בְּבַת אַחַת וּבַחֲדָא הַתְרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא is about eating both גידין at once after a single warning, and the תנא קמא still gives eighty.

steps.title: Who is the תנא קמא? Not the רבנן who argue with סומכוס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the תנא קמא is. It cannot be the רבנן who argue with סומכוס: they give only one set of lashes even for separate animals, so all the more so here.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא קמא? If you say it is the רבנן who argue with סומכוס, then if there, where the bodies are separate, the רבנן exempt from the second set, here, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא gives eighty lashes for one eating with one warning, and rules out the רבנן of the earlier מחלוקת with סומכוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case, the animals were clearly separate bodies (גופין מוחלקין), yet the רבנן did not give a second set of lashes. Here the two גידין are eaten in one act, which is even less separate. So by a כל שכן the רבנן would surely give only forty here, and the תנא קמא who says eighty cannot be them.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
Who disagree with him
Separate bodies, here separate animals
They exempt
All the more so

phrases.english: Who is the first tanna?
If we say it is the Rabbis
who disagree with Sumakhos,
phrases.notes: This is the earlier משנה about אותו ואת בנו, slaughtering a mother animal and its young.

phrases.english: then if there, where the bodies are separate,
the Rabbis exempt him,
phrases.notes: Exempt from a second set of lashes.

phrases.english: here, is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא קַמָּא? אִילֵימָא רַבָּנַן דִּפְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּסוֹמְכוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the case just defined to identify who holds the eighty-lashes view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds the eighty-lashes view in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the תנא קמא is the רבנן who disagree with סומכוס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כל שכן: the רבנן exempt from a second set even with separate animals, so they would surely exempt when it is one act of eating.

steps.title: So the תנא קמא must be סומכוס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the תנא קמא is סומכוס. So סומכוס gives two sets of lashes for two forbidden items eaten under one warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not סומכוס?
steps.whatsHappening: Having ruled out the רבנן, the גמרא concludes that the eighty-lashes view belongs to סומכוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תנא קמא is סומכוס, then סומכוס gives eighty even when both items are eaten at once after one warning. That would answer the question of how סומכוס counts lashes under a single warning. The next step, however, rejects this proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not...? (introduces the conclusion the גמרא is pushing toward)

steps.whatToRemember: At this point the גמרא's proof reads the two-גידין ברייתא as one eating with one warning. On that reading, its eighty-lashes view must be סומכוס. The next step pushes back on this proof.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not Sumakhos!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו סוֹמְכוֹס הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion after the רבנן were ruled out.
steps.raayaObject: סומכוס gives two sets of lashes for two forbidden eatings under a single warning.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The two-גידין ברייתא, whose תנא קמא gives eighty even for one act with one warning.

steps.title: The case is really one after the other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof that the תנא קמא is סומכוס. The case can be eating the two גידין one after the other. רבי יהודה says only forty because one גיד was less than a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he ate them one after the other. And as for your question, 'What is רבי יהודה's reason?': it is a case where one of them does not have a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 7 by explaining the ברייתא in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said that if he ate them one after the other, רבי יהודה's 'only forty' makes no sense. Now the גמרא answers that רבי יהודה has his own reason: one גיד was smaller than a כזית, so it does not count. With that, the ברייתא no longer proves anything about סומכוס.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually. It signals going back to an option that was rejected earlier.
One after the other, with a separate warning for each.
An olive's size. This is the usual minimum amount of food that makes a person liable for eating.

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not say סומכוס is wrong. It only shows that this ברייתא cannot prove what סומכוס holds.

phrases.english: Actually, it is a case of one after the other,
phrases.notes: This is the option Step 4 rejected: each גיד was eaten separately, with its own warning.

phrases.english: And as for what you said: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?
It is a case where there is not an olive-bulk in it,
phrases.notes: He means one of the two גידין was smaller than a כזית.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undoes the conclusion of Step 7 by reviving the case that Step 4 had rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that the תנא קמא of the ברייתא is סומכוס.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed רבי יהודה's 'forty' could only make sense if both גידין were eaten at once. But he may simply hold that a piece smaller than a כזית does not count.

steps.title: רבי יהודה requires an olive-bulk for גיד הנשה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה holds a person is not liable for a גיד הנשה unless it is a כזית. The תנא קמא holds he is liable for a whole גיד even if it is smaller.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: If he ate it and it does not have a כזית, he is liable. רבי יהודה says he is not liable unless it has a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that רבי יהודה really holds the view Step 8 gave him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא treats a whole גיד as something that counts on its own, whatever its size. רבי יהודה requires the normal minimum of a כזית. So in the two-גיד case, one small גיד adds nothing for him, and he gives only forty lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable to punishment. Here it means forty lashes.
Not until it contains, meaning he is liable only if it has that amount.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of the two גידי הנשה cannot prove that סומכוס gives two sets of lashes. It can be explained as eating one after the other, with רבי יהודה disagreeing only because of the size of a כזית.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
If one ate it and it does not have an olive-bulk, he is liable;
phrases.notes: 'It' is a whole גיד הנשה eaten completely.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ כְּזַיִת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Not unless it has an olive-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in Step 8 with a source.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה holds a גיד הנשה smaller than a כזית does not make a person liable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about eating a גיד הנשה that is less than a כזית.

steps.title: Four days a year the seller must tell the buyer
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: on four festival eves, a person selling an animal must tell the buyer if he already sold its mother or its daughter to be slaughtered. רבי יוסי הגלילי adds ערב יום הכפורים in the גליל.
steps.simpleTranslation: On four occasions in the year, someone who sells an animal must tell the buyer, 'I sold its mother to be slaughtered' or 'I sold its daughter to be slaughtered.' These are: the eve of the last יום טוב of סוכות, the eve of the first day of פסח, ערב עצרת, and ערב ראש השנה. According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, also ערב יום הכפורים in the גליל.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a rule: on certain busy days, a seller must warn the buyer that the mother or the offspring of this animal was already sold for slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On these days almost everyone slaughters right away for the festival meal. So two buyers might slaughter a mother and its offspring on the same day, which breaks אותו ואת בנו. The warning lets the second buyer wait a day.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה.
Four set times in the year.
To inform him.
The ban on slaughtering a mother animal and its offspring on the same day.
שבועות.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the seller shares responsibility to keep the buyer from breaking the איסור of אותו ואת בנו.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
On four occasions in the year,
one who sells an animal to his fellow
must inform him:
"I sold its mother to be slaughtered,"
"I sold its daughter to be slaughtered."
And these are they:

phrases.aramaic: עֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חַג,
phrases.english: The eve of the last festival day of the Festival,
phrases.notes: 'The Festival' here means סוכות, so this is the day before שמיני עצרת.

phrases.aramaic: וְעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח,
phrases.english: and the eve of the first festival day of Passover,
and the eve of Shavuot, and the eve of Rosh HaShana.
And according to the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
also the eve of Yom Kippur in the Galilee.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בְּאַרְבָּעָה פְּרָקִים בַּשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of סומכוס ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On four festival eves, a seller must tell the buyer that he sold the mother or the offspring of this animal for slaughter.

steps.title: רבי יהודה limits the duty to inform
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the seller must inform only when there was no gap between the two sales. He agrees that a sale to a groom and a bride always needs a warning, since they will both slaughter on the same day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: When must he inform? When there was no gap between the sales. But if there was a gap, he does not need to inform. And רבי יהודה agrees that if he sold the mother to the חתן and the daughter to the כלה, he must inform, because it is known they will both slaughter on one day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה narrows the rule of the משנה, and then names one case where he agrees the warning is always needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first animal was sold on an earlier day, we assume that buyer already slaughtered it on that day, so the second buyer is not at risk. A חתן and a כלה are different: both are preparing for the same wedding feast. So they will surely slaughter on the same day, even if they bought on different days.

keyTerms.meaning: When? It introduces a limit on a rule.
A gap of time between the two sales.
And he agrees.
A groom and a bride.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: When?
At a time when he has no gap,
phrases.notes: He means the mother and the offspring were sold on the same day.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יֵשׁ לוֹ רֶיוַח – אֵין צָרִיךְ לְהוֹדִיעוֹ.
phrases.english: but if he has a gap, he does not need to inform him.
And Rabbi Yehuda agrees

phrases.aramaic: בְּמוֹכֵר אֶת הָאֵם לֶחָתָן וְאֶת הַבַּת לַכַּלָּה –
phrases.english: in a case where one sells the mother to the groom and the daughter to the bride,
that he must inform him,
since it is known that both of them slaughter on one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: אֵימָתַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule of the משנה in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The warning is needed only if both animals were sold on the same day. A sale to a חתן and a כלה always needs a warning.

steps.title: On these days the butcher can be forced to slaughter
steps.stepSummary: On the four festival eves, a butcher can be forced to slaughter even a costly ox for a buyer who paid only one דינר. Because of this, if the ox dies, the loss falls on the buyer. On other days the loss falls on the seller.
steps.simpleTranslation: On these four occasions we force the butcher to slaughter against his will. Even if the ox is worth a thousand דינרים and the buyer has only one דינר in it, we force him to slaughter. So if it dies, it dies at the buyer's loss. But on the rest of the days of the year it is not so, so if it dies, it dies at the seller's loss.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds another special law for these four days: the butcher can be forced to slaughter, and this changes who loses money if the animal dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the butcher must slaughter for the buyer no matter what, the buyer's single דינר is treated as already locked into the sale. So if the ox dies first, the buyer loses his money. On regular days the butcher does not have to slaughter, so the sale is not final, and the seller takes the loss.

keyTerms.meaning: A butcher.
Against his will.
We force him, meaning בית דין makes him do it.
The buyer.
The seller.

steps.whatToRemember: On the four festival eves, the seller must warn about אותו ואת בנו, the butcher can be forced to slaughter, and the risk of the animal dying shifts to the buyer.

phrases.english: On these four occasions
we make the butcher slaughter against his will;
even if an ox is worth a thousand dinars
and the buyer has only a dinar in it,
phrases.notes: The buyer paid for just one דינר's worth of meat from the ox.

phrases.english: we force him to slaughter.
Therefore, if it dies, it dies at the buyer's loss.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּשְׁאָר יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה אֵינוֹ כֵּן,
phrases.english: But on the rest of the days of the year it is not so;
therefore, if it dies, it dies at the seller's loss.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאַרְבָּעָה פְּרָקִים אֵלּוּ מַשְׁחִיטִין אֶת הַטַּבָּח בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second special law for the same four occasions listed in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the four festival eves, a butcher is forced to slaughter, and the risk of the animal dying falls on the buyer. On other days it falls on the seller.

steps.title: If the seller did not warn him, the buyer may slaughter
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if the seller gave no warning, the buyer may go ahead and slaughter without worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: if the seller did not tell him, the buyer goes and slaughters and does not hold back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that adds to the משנה's rule that the seller must tell the buyer about an earlier sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה put the job of warning on the seller. So the buyer does not need to ask questions. If the seller said nothing, the buyer may assume the mother or daughter was not sold for slaughter that day.

keyTerms.meaning: he told him or informed him
he does not need to hold back

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the seller's silence counts as a sign the buyer can rely on.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
if he did not inform him,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the seller, and 'him' is the buyer from the משנה.

phrases.english: he goes and slaughters and does not refrain.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא, אִם לֹא הוֹדִיעוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה from steps 10-12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without a warning from the seller, the buyer may slaughter with no worry.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say mother to the groom and daughter to the bride?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה's case names exactly which animal went to the groom and which went to the bride.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'רבי יהודה says: When...' Why do I need it to teach 'the mother to the groom and the daughter to the bride'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's words in the משנה and asks about the wording of the groom-and-bride case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law would be the same if it said 'one to the groom and one to the bride.' So why did the משנה say which animal went to which side? The גמרא assumes the extra detail must be teaching something.

keyTerms.meaning: when? (the opening word of רבי יהודה's statement in the משנה)
why do I need it to teach? A question about extra wording.
groom
bride

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: When?
Why do I need to teach
the mother to the groom
and the daughter to the bride?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי לְמִיתְנֵי אֶת הָאֵם לֶחָתָן וְאֶת הַבַּת לַכַּלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the משנה say which animal went to the groom and which went to the bride?

steps.title: The groom's side does more of the work
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is teaching a side lesson: it is normal for the groom's family to do more than the bride's family.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is teaching us something along the way: it is normal for the groom's household to work harder than the bride's household.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the wording teaches a lesson about everyday life, in addition to the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother animal is bigger, so it goes to the groom's side. This shows that the groom's family usually puts in more effort for the wedding. The law of the warning does not change.

keyTerms.meaning: a lesson taught in passing
normal, proper conduct
to put in effort

phrases.english: A matter along the way
it teaches us:
that it is proper conduct
for the groom's household to exert itself
more than the bride's household.
phrases.notes: The mother is the bigger animal, so the groom's side buys the bigger one.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִלְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָמַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wording teaches that the groom's family normally makes the bigger effort.

steps.title: How can the buyer lose if he never pulled the ox?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the loss can fall on the buyer during the four festival eves if he never did משיכה on the ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'On these four occasions...' if the ox dies, it dies at the buyer's loss. But he did not pull it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule from step 12 that the buyer carries the loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying money alone does not acquire a movable item. The buyer must pull it (משיכה). If the buyer never pulled the ox, it still belongs to the seller. So why should the buyer lose when it dies?

keyTerms.meaning: pulling an object, which is the act that acquires movable items
the four festival eves listed in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Under the usual rule of the חכמים, money alone does not acquire a movable item; pulling it (משיכה) does. That is why paying the דינר seems not to be enough. Step 21 shows that by Torah law money does acquire.

phrases.english: 'On these four occasions,'
phrases.notes: These are the משנה's words. The rule being questioned is that the ox dies at the buyer's loss.

phrases.english: But he did not pull it!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאַרְבָּעָה פְּרָקִים אֵלּוּ, וְהָא לֹא מָשַׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ox case from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that the buyer carries the loss on the four festival eves
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without משיכה the buyer never acquired the ox, so its death should not be his loss.

steps.title: רב: the buyer did pull the ox
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the משנה is talking about a buyer who did pull the ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב: it is a case where he pulled it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the challenge by saying the משנה is about a case where the buyer did משיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the buyer pulled the ox, he owns it. Then it makes sense that he takes the loss when it dies.

keyTerms.meaning: in a case where he pulled it

phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rav said:
Where he pulled it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: כְּשֶׁמָּשַׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The buyer never acquired the ox.
steps.terutzMaskana: The buyer pulled the ox and acquired it.

steps.title: But the second half says the seller loses
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the משנה says that on other days the seller loses. That cannot fit a buyer who pulled the ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end of the משנה: 'But on the rest of the days of the year it is not so. Therefore, if it dies, it dies at the seller's loss.' But he pulled it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's answer using the second half of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the buyer pulled the ox, he owns it on any day of the year. So the seller should never carry the loss. Yet the משנה says that on ordinary days the seller does lose, so רב's case cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: if so
the second or later part of a משנה
seller

phrases.english: If so, say the latter clause:
But during the rest of the days of the year
it is not so;
therefore if it dies, it dies at the seller's loss.
But he pulled it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's answer in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that the buyer pulled the ox
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the ox is pulled, the buyer owns it on every day, so the seller could never lose. This goes against the סיפא.

steps.title: Someone else acquired the meat for the buyer
steps.stepSummary: The buyer did not pull the ox. Someone else acquired it for him. That works only when it helps him, which is on a festival eve.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר רב יצחק said: really, he did not pull it. The case is where the seller gave him ownership through another person. On these four occasions, it helps him, and you can act for a person's benefit when he is not there. On the rest of the days of the year, it hurts him, and you cannot act against a person when he is not there.
steps.whatsHappening: A new answer explains both halves of the משנה: the buyer did not pull the ox himself, but someone else acquired the meat for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One person can acquire something for another without asking him, but only if it helps him (זכין לאדם שלא בפניו). Before a festival the buyer wants the meat, so the purchase helps him and he carries the loss. On ordinary days, owning meat from an ox that is not yet slaughtered only puts him at risk, so the purchase does not take effect and the seller loses.

keyTerms.meaning: really, in truth (going back to the first way of seeing the case)
gave him ownership through another person
you can acquire something for a person who is not there if it helps him
you cannot do something that hurts a person when he is not there

steps.whatToRemember: The same act of acquiring through someone else works on a festival eve, because it helps the buyer. It does not work on other days, because it hurts him. That is why the loss falls on different people in the two halves of the משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: זכין לאדם שלא בפניו is a basic rule of acquiring for others. This step shows that one act can help a person at one time and hurt him at another.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said:
Actually, it is where he did not pull it,
and it is a case where he gave him ownership
by means of another person.
phrases.notes: The seller had a third person acquire a דינר's worth of the meat for the buyer, without asking the buyer first.

phrases.english: On these four occasions,
where it is a benefit for him,
one may act for a person's benefit in his absence.
During the rest of the days of the year,
where it is a disadvantage for him,
one may not act to a person's disadvantage in his absence.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא מָשַׁךְ, וּכְגוֹן שֶׁזִּיכָּה לוֹ עַל יְדֵי אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets aside רב's answer and answers both step 16 and step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case so both halves of the משנה fit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The buyer pulled the ox himself, which cannot explain the סיפא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Someone else acquired the meat for the buyer. This works only when it benefits him, which is on the festival eves.

steps.title: On the four festival eves, the Sages kept Torah law
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי יוחנן, gives a different answer: on the four festival eves the חכמים let the Torah law stand, and under Torah law money acquires.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says that רבי יוחנן said: On these four occasions, the Sages based their ruling on Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the question of how the buyer can lose the ox without pulling it. On the four festival eves, the חכמים kept the plain Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the answers said the buyer did משיכה, or that someone else acquired the ox for him. Here there is no need for either one. On these four days the buyer's money by itself acquires the animal, so if it dies, it is his loss.

keyTerms.meaning: Four set times of the year (the four festival eves in the משנה)
They set their ruling (they based their law on...)
Torah law, before any rabbinic changes

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the חכמים made a new rule for the festivals. They held back their usual rule (that only משיכה acquires), so the original Torah law applies again.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says, Rabbi Yochanan said:
On these four occasions
phrases.notes: These are the four festival eves from the משנה, when the butcher is forced to slaughter.

phrases.english: the Sages established their ruling
on Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from Steps 17 and 19 to the question in Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different legal mechanism: money acquires on these days, so no משיכה is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without משיכה, the buyer cannot own the ox, so the loss should not be his.
steps.terutzMaskana: On the four festival eves, Torah law applies and the buyer's payment acquires the ox.

steps.title: By Torah law money acquires; pulling is a rabbinic rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites רבי יוחנן's known view: by Torah law money acquires. The חכמים required משיכה so the seller would keep watching the goods.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said: By Torah law, money acquires. Why did the Sages say that pulling acquires? It is a decree, so that the seller will not say to the buyer, 'Your wheat burned in the attic.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source behind the last step. It shows that רבי יוחנן holds that by Torah law money acquires, and that משיכה is only a rabbinic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If money acquires at once, the seller no longer owns the goods. He might then not bother to save them from a fire and just tell the buyer it was his loss. So the חכמים said ownership passes only when the buyer pulls the item. On the festival eves, the need for meat for the festival is more important, so the חכמים let the Torah law apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Money acquires (paying makes the item yours)
Pulling the item, a way to acquire movable things
A protective rule made by the חכמים
An upper room or attic

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule for buying movable things in דיני ממונות: by Torah law money acquires, but the חכמים require משיכה.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said:
By Torah law, money acquires,
and why did they say pulling acquires?
It is a decree, in case he says to him
phrases.notes: 'He' is the seller, who already has the money, speaking to the buyer.

phrases.english: 'Your wheat burned in the attic.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the background that explains the ruling in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the חכמים could fall back on Torah law on the festival eves
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's statement that by Torah law money acquires, and משיכה is only a rabbinic decree

steps.title: For אותו ואת בנו, the day follows the night
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: for the law of not slaughtering a mother and its young on the same day, the 'day' begins with the night before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The 'one day' stated about an animal and its young means that the day follows the night.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It explains how to count the 'one day' in the law of אותו ואת בנו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'one day' starts at nightfall and runs through the next daytime. So if you slaughter the mother at night, you may not slaughter its young the next day, because both are the same 'day'. If you slaughter it in the daytime, you may slaughter the young that night, because a new day has started.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal and its young, which may not be slaughtered on the same day
'One day', the Torah's words for this time limit
The day follows the night (night comes first in the day)

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ ״יוֹם אֶחָד״ הָאָמוּר בְּאוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ –
phrases.english: Mishnah: The 'one day' stated about an animal and its young:
the day follows the night.
phrases.notes: So the night and the daytime after it count together as one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ ״יוֹם אֶחָד״ הָאָמוּר בְּאוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the butcher discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For אותו ואת בנו, a day is counted from nightfall through the following daytime.

steps.title: בן זומא learns it from the creation story
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן זומא proves the rule by comparing the words 'one day' in the creation story with the same words in אותו ואת בנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן זומא expounded this: 'One day' is said about Creation, and 'one day' is said about an animal and its young. Just as in Creation the day follows the night, so too with an animal and its young the day follows the night.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the source for its rule. The same words 'one day' show up in two places in the Torah, so they work the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בראשית it says 'there was evening and there was morning, one day', so evening comes first. Since אותו ואת בנו uses the same words, 'one day', it is counted the same way: night first, then day. This kind of learning from matching words is called a גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Expounded, learned something from the verses
The story of Creation
Learning one law from another because the Torah uses the same words in both

phrases.aramaic: אֶת זוֹ דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן זוֹמָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Zoma expounded this:
It is stated in the act of Creation 'one day',
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:5

phrases.english: and it is stated about an animal and its young 'one day'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:28

phrases.english: Just as with the 'one day' stated in the act of Creation
the day follows the night,

phrases.aramaic: אַף ״יוֹם אֶחָד״ הָאָמוּר בְּאוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ
phrases.english: so too with the 'one day' stated about an animal and its young
the day follows the night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶת זוֹ דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן זוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the Torah source for the rule in Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that for אותו ואת בנו the day follows the night
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה between 'one day' in Creation (בראשית 1:5) and in אותו ואת בנו (ויקרא 22:28)

steps.title: Why we might have counted it like קדשים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains why בן זומא needed his proof. The section is about קדשים, where the night follows the day, so we might have counted אותו ואת בנו that way too.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The רבנן taught: רבי שמעון בן זומא expounded this because the whole section speaks only about sacrificial animals, and with sacrificial animals the night follows the day. You might think this is the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains why the proof was needed. It first describes the mistake we might have made. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of אותו ואת בנו appears in the middle of a Torah section about קרבנות. For קרבנות, time counts from the day forward, so the night after the day goes with it. So we might have thought the 'one day' here also starts in the morning.

keyTerms.meaning: The topic or section of the Torah
Sacrificial animals, קרבנות
The night follows the day (the day comes first)
'You might think...', which brings up a possible mistake

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two phrases. Here it is 'night follows the day', which is the rule for קדשים. The rule for אותו ואת בנו is the reverse: 'the day follows the night'.

phrases.english: Gemara: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֶת זוֹ דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן זוֹמָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Zoma expounded this,
because the entire section
speaks only about sacrificial animals,
and with sacrificial animals the night follows the day,
phrases.notes: In other words, for a קרבן the night after a day still belongs to that day.

phrases.english: you might think this one is the same?

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֶת זוֹ דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן זוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the proof in Step 23 was needed by showing the mistake it prevents.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether אותו ואת בנו should be counted like קדשים, with the day first and then the night

steps.title: The creation story settles it: night comes first
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers with the גזירה שוה from Creation: just as there the day follows the night, so too in אותו ואת בנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says here 'one day', and it says in Creation 'one day'. Just as in Creation the day follows the night, so too with an animal and its young the day follows the night.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own 'you might think'. The matching words 'one day' tie this law to Creation and not to the rules of קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section's topic would point to counting like קדשים, but the matching words are stronger. So אותו ואת בנו follows the normal order of days, starting at night. This applies to all animals, both regular ones and קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is stated here', the first half of a גזירה שוה
'So too', which applies the first case to the second

steps.whatToRemember: For אותו ואת בנו, a 'day' runs from nightfall to the end of the next daytime, like the days of Creation. This holds even though the פסוק is in a section about קדשים, where the night follows the day.

phrases.english: It is stated here 'one day',
and it is stated in the act of Creation 'one day'.
Just as with the 'one day' stated in the act of Creation
the day follows the night,

phrases.aramaic: אַף יוֹם הָאָמוּר בְּאוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ –
phrases.english: so too with the day stated about an animal and its young
the day follows the night.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״יוֹם אֶחָד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the possible mistake raised in Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The גזירה שוה with Creation shows that for אותו ואת בנו the day follows the night, not like קדשים.
